# Corio / Commerce One License and Hosting Agreement – Reference Notes

No amendments were provided; this is the original agreement only.

**Parties/Date:** Corio Inc. (Delaware; 700 Bay Road, Suite 210, Redwood City, CA 94063) and Commerce One, Inc. (Delaware; 1600 Rivera Ave., Walnut Creek, CA 94596). Effective Oct 29, 1999. Corio signed 11/5/99 (George Kadifa, CEO); Commerce One's signer (Mark Biestman, VP Worldwide Sales) is undated.

**Software:** Hosted BuySite v6.0 (object code only), plus MarketSite.net Service access. Exhibit A relationship/product managers are blank.

**Licenses (§2):** Hosting license is fee-bearing, perpetual, irrevocable, nonexclusive, nontransferable (except per §14.1), Territory only. Corio may sublicense an unlimited number of Customers, hosted only. Internal-use and demo licenses are royalty-free. Distribution license (§2.4) lets Corio resell Commerce One licenses; Commerce One must refer direct inquiries to Corio. No source code is delivered. Commerce One keeps ownership (§2.8). Reverse engineering is barred (§2.7). Updates/Upgrades are included in maintenance fees (§2.9).
- **Territory:** North America. Corio may seek worldwide expansion at no added cost; Commerce One may not unreasonably withhold (§2.10).
- **Corio Market Segment:** customers with annual revenue under $1,000,000,000 (entity or separately reporting division). Existing customers that outgrow it may continue.

**Acceptance (§3.1):** Test within 30 days of delivery, no later than Dec 1, 1999. Commerce One has 15 days to fix defects. Up to three tests, and all testing must be done by Dec 30, 1999, with written notice by Dec 31, 1999. After the third failure, Corio may repeat the test or terminate with a refund of fees paid.

**Fees (Exh. B; dollar figures redacted [*]):**
- License fee due on acceptance.
- Annual maintenance is Net 30 from the acceptance anniversary.
- MarketSite access fee is due on acceptance and each anniversary.
- Revenue share is paid quarterly, net 30 after quarter close. Commerce One pays Corio [*] of MarketSite transaction fees; Corio pays Commerce One [*] of Application Management Revenue.
- No revenue share is due on the initial 3000 Software User licenses (minimum 40 users per Customer). Professional service and network fees are excluded. Accrual begins at the Customer's live operations.
- Implementation is time and materials, capped at [*]; Net 30 after milestone invoices.
- Corio pays taxes other than on Commerce One's income (§4.3).
- Audit (§4.4): records kept 3 years; inspection once per calendar year by an independent CPA; Commerce One bears the cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, in which case Corio reimburses.

**Services:** One full-time operations consultant for one week free (§5.1). Professional services for the first 3 implementations (§5.2). Quarterly product meetings (§5.4). Support per Exh. C: Mon–Fri 7am–7pm PST, 24x7 for Priority 1; up to 5 registered contacts; P1 action plan in 2 hours, P2 in 4 hours; attempted contact within 30 minutes of a critical incident. Corio handles routine Customer support. Support continues after termination if annual fees are paid (§5.3). Engineering access is free (§13.3).

**Warranties:** Commerce One warrants IP ownership and non-infringement (§7.2). Product warranty runs 60 days from the Effective Date, no later than Dec 31, 1999. The remedy is correction/replacement, or termination with refund of prepaid fees, as the sole remedy (§7.3). Y2K warranty (§7.4).

**Indemnity (§8):** Commerce One indemnifies Corio and its Customers for third-party IP claims. Its options are to procure rights, replace/modify, or terminate with a pro-rated refund.

**Liability cap (§9):** Fees paid for the relevant transaction in the 12 months before the claim. Consequential damages and lost profits are excluded. Both exclude §8 indemnity liability.

**Term (§11):** 5 years initially, then automatic 1-year renewals unless 30 days' written notice before expiry. Termination for material breach not cured within 30 days; immediate termination on insolvency. Corio's existing Customers keep access post-termination. Surviving sections: 4.2, 5.3, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 14.

**Escrow (§12):** Escrow agreement within 60 days of the Effective Date, held in California, at Corio's cost. Release if Commerce One dissolves or ceases business, or has a repeated material support breach uncured for 60 days. Disputes: 10 business days of officer negotiation, then arbitration. Post-release license is limited to support and maintenance.

**Other:** Confidentiality governed by a separate NDA (§10). Ownership of Developments goes to Corio unless Commerce One supports them (§13.5); mutual patent covenant not to sue (§13.6). Assignment requires consent, except for merger or asset sale, but consent is needed if the other party is a direct competitor (§14.1). California law (CISG excluded); binding AAA arbitration, one arbitrator, San Francisco County; loser pays AAA fees (§14.3). Notice: personal delivery, overnight courier (1 day), certified mail (5 days). Corio may subcontract (§14.8). §365(n) bankruptcy protection (§14.9). Entire agreement clause (§14.10). Amendments must be in writing and signed (§14.2).

**Exh. D (non-binding):** Quarterly relationship meetings; marketing fund within 6 months; one dedicated employee each; Corio to use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain 2 initial Customer orders within 60 days.

# Reference Notes: PcoMed / Integra Supply Agreement (no amendments provided)

**Parties & date:** Integra LifeSciences Corporation (Delaware; 311 Enterprise Drive, Plainsboro, NJ 08536) and PcoMed, LLC (Colorado LLC; 105 S. Sunset St., Longmont, CO 80501). Effective Date May 15, 2013. Signed by PcoMed (Steve Jacobs, CEO) May 15, 2013 and Integra (Brian Larkin, President) May 29, 2013. Affiliates named include SeaSpine and Theken Spine.

**Purpose:** PcoMed applies its surface modification technology (osteoconductive titanium molecular modification of PEEK/PEKK/PAEK) to Integra's implantable spinal interbody/intervertebral devices. Field = spinal interbody/intervertebral surgical methods (fusion, spacer, arthroplasty).

**Exclusivity (§3):** PcoMed grants Integra and Affiliates a sole, exclusive worldwide right to sell/commercialize treated Integra Products in the Field. No right to manufacture with the technology. PcoMed may not sell or license to third parties in the Field. Integra may not apply other coatings (except for identification or sterilization) or impair the technology's integrity (§3.3).
- **Conversion to non-exclusive (§3.2):** If Integra misses Minimum Payments, fails to pay under §2.1-2.3, or otherwise defaults, PcoMed may convert at its sole discretion after written notice and a **45-day cure** period.
- **Territory (§1.27):** Worldwide for 36 months after Notice of Initial Acceptance of First Product Order; thereafter PcoMed may exclude the PRC if Integra has no sales there, on **60 days'** written notice of intent to use a third-party marketer.

**Money:**
- Milestones: first payment on execution; second within 30 days after Notice of Initial Acceptance (amounts redacted). First Product Order due within 60 days of Effective Date. Acceptance notice issued within 10 business days of receiving conforming product.
- Fees: percent of Net Sales of Treated and Partially Treated Products, with a higher or different rate depending on exclusive vs. non-exclusive status at time of sale (all rates redacted). Paid quarterly within **45 days** after quarter end, with a statement. Payments in USD.
- Net Sales deductions: discounts, commissions, returns, taxes/duties, freight/insurance; excludes clinical trial sales.
- Run Fee: flat fee per run (redacted) for max **100** products per run. No Run Fee for regulatory testing quantities (up to a redacted number of units or **four** runs). Due within **30 days** of each run.
- Minimum Payments (Attachment B): seven one-year periods starting at acceptance of First Product Order; amounts redacted. Due annually within **45 days** after period end. Integra uses commercially reasonable efforts; it may satisfy shortfalls by elective cash payment. PcoMed's **sole remedy** for a shortfall is conversion to non-exclusive; Integra has no liability.
- Fee offset: Integra may offset up to a redacted percentage of third-party settlement/license costs caused by PcoMed. Reduced fees still count fully toward Minimums.
- Audit (§6.2): once per calendar year, independent CPA chosen by PcoMed, at PcoMed's cost; results reported within 60 days; underpayments paid within 60 days of agreement or final judgment.
- Taxes (§6.3): PcoMed bears taxes on its receipts; Integra withholds where required.

**Term (§4):** Initial Term runs from Effective Date to the due date of Minimum Payment Period 7 payment. Renewal only by mutual written agreement. Termination for material breach: **60 days'** notice and cure (or an acceptable cure plan). Immediate termination on bankruptcy/insolvency. After early termination (except for Integra breach of §5 or §8), Integra gets an **18-month** sell-off of inventory and committed components. Surviving sections: 2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 4.4(c), 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12.

**Confidentiality (§5):** Term plus **20 years**. Agreement terms confidential, with exceptions for legal filings, advisors, and financing/M&A/litigation. Injunctive relief available without bond. Each party submits its own regulatory data to regulators.

**IP (§8):** Each party keeps its own technology. Joint inventions go to PcoMed if primarily relating to PcoMed Technology, and to Integra if primarily relating to Integra Products. PcoMed controls patent filing and prosecution at its expense. Enforcement: PcoMed has first right on matters exclusively about its technology (90 days to respond to Integra's request; Integra may require action if PcoMed fails to act within 90 days or 6 months). Integra has the sole right on other infringement. Declaratory judgment defense: the other party may intervene within 30 days.

**Liability and indemnity:** Mutual exclusion of special, consequential, incidental and indirect damages, except for breaches of §3.1, §5, and §§8.1-8.2. PcoMed indemnifies for infringement from its technology, breach of its reps, and product defects from its technology (Integra's recovery for infringement costs is by fee offset only). Integra indemnifies for infringement from Integra Technology, breach of its reps, and Integra product defects.

**Misc.:** Governing law: **New Jersey**. Disputes: 30-day senior-officer negotiation, then binding arbitration in **Denver, Colorado** (Judicial Arbiter Group, 3-person panel, AAA rules, each side bears own costs). Assignment needs consent, except to an Affiliate or in a merger/sale of substantially all related assets. Force majeure excludes payment obligations. Modifications require a signed, dated writing. Notice to PcoMed's counsel: Alan Keeffe, Sherman & Howard LLC, Steamboat Springs, CO. Integra may state the products were partly manufactured by PcoMed.

# Reference Notes: Purolator / Parcelway (Dynamex) Marketing & Transportation Services Agreement

**Date:** Nov 20, 1995. **Parties:** Purolator Courier Ltd. and Parcelway Courier Systems Canada Ltd. (subsidiary of Dynamex Inc.), "Dynamex". No amendments provided. Independent contractors (s.33: no partnership, JV, agency or employment).

**Term/Termination**
- Indefinite term (2.1).
- Without cause: **2 years'** written notice (19.1).
- Change in control of a party: other party may terminate on prior written notice (19.2).
- Reputation harm: other party may terminate on notice it deems appropriate (41).
- Default termination (17.2(a)): **120 days'** written notice; immediate on written notice for 17.1(g) (service failure) and (h) (uncured breach).

**Scope**
- Purolator sells sameday service under its name and tenders all sameday requests to Dynamex, bills the customer. Dynamex sells overnight service under its name, tenders all next-day/multi-day requests to Purolator, bills the customer. Each invoices the other at Schedule D (Purolator pays Dynamex) and Schedule E (Dynamex pays Purolator) rates.
- Territory: Canada and US (3.11). Similar agreements with third parties require prior written consent; Dynamex may contract with others in the US if that doesn't prevent service to Purolator.
- On-time performance: at least **90%**, measured monthly; failure = Monthly Service Failure (3.4).
- Non-solicitation of each other's customers (3.5, 3.6), except joint marketing.
- Dynamex may not provide sameday service for other next-day/multi-day carriers (3.9). Exception: Alltours customers, capped at **$5,000/month** revenue, and only if no change in control of Alltours.
- Purolator's DMS (Distribution Management Services Inc.) and Dynamex's mail room/building distribution services are carved out (3.10).
- Schedules A, B (service standards), C (Operational Plan; monthly operational meetings), D, E (rates), F (security).

**Payment**
- Invoices twice monthly (15th and last day), with supporting documentation (bills of lading not required). Delivered within 3 days of invoicing; payable net **15 days**.
- Interest at CIBC (Toronto Main Branch) prime on amounts overdue **30+ days**.
- Debit/credit notes: pay net 15 days from receipt and acceptance.
- Services zero-rated for GST (interlining), Excise Tax Act Sch. VI, Part VII, s.1 (5.8). Currency is Canadian; business days per Ontario.

**Liability/Indemnity/Insurance**
- Party liable for loss, damage or delay to Freight in its care, custody or control; not liable if damage is solely from improper packing (6.1). Investigation report due within **30 days** (6.2).
- Liability capped at the other party's liability to its customers: **$4.41/kg or $2.00/lb** unless higher value declared (6.3).
- Claims paid within **45 days** of documentation, otherwise set-off right (7.1).
- Mutual indemnity, even if the indemnitee's negligence is involved (8.1), but capped at the insurance coverage in s.9 (8.2).
- Insurance: cargo liability min **$100,000** per occurrence; auto/CGL/property min **$2,000,000** per occurrence. Other party as additional insured, cross-liability, waiver of subrogation. Certificates before start and annually; **30 days'** notice of cancellation or change. Subcontractors must carry equivalent cover (9).
- Dangerous goods: Transportation of Dangerous Goods Act, S.C. 1992, c.34. A party is liable only if it had actual prior knowledge. Training certificates required; failure allows immediate termination (13).

**Default/Penalties**
- More than **3** Monthly Performance Failures in any 12 months = Event of Default (16.1, 17.1(g)).
- Other defaults: bankruptcy petition not dismissed within **60 days**; insolvency; ceasing business; uncured breach after **30 days'** notice (17.1).
- Remedies: terminate, recover monies, retake property/Freight without court order (17.2); cumulative (37).
- Penalty (18.1): **5 × (90% − actual %) × shipments × other party's average yield**. Example: 5 × (90−85) × 100 × $10 = **$250**.
- Strike: the affected party must try to subcontract the services; it is then not in default under 17.1(c) (15).

**Other**
- Force majeure (s.22): immediate written notice, confirmed in writing.
- Non-compete after termination: **6 months** after default termination; **12 months** for the party whose control changed (19.2) (42).
- Assignment or subcontracting requires prior written consent (23). Contents confidential (23.2, 34). Public announcements mutually agreed (38).
- Order of precedence: Agreement, Schedules, then operating plan (24.2). Amendments in writing signed by both (27). Time of the essence (30).
- Governing law: **Ontario**; courts of Ontario (36).
- Arbitration (39): single arbitrator appointed within **10 business days**, otherwise by the President of the Arbitrators' Institute of Canada Inc.; held in Metropolitan Toronto under the Arbitration Act; final and binding; costs split equally; a condition precedent to suit.
- Notices (20): hand, mail (deemed received 5 business days), fax/electronic. Purolator: 5995 Avebury Rd, Suite 500, Mississauga, ON L5R 3T8. Dynamex: 2630 Skymark Ave, Suite 610, Mississauga, ON L4W 5A4.
- Drafting quirks: the non-competition section is numbered 32.1 in the text but is 42.1; s.20.2 is mislabelled and is Purolator's warranties; the signature blocks are illegible.

# Reference Notes: VIP–BNL Outsourcing Agreement (no amendments provided)

**Parties/Date:** Virtual Item Processing Systems, Inc. (VIP; Oklahoma corp., 2525 NW Expressway, Ste 105, Oklahoma City, OK 73112) and Brokers National Life Assurance Company (BNL; Arkansas-domiciled insurer, 7010 Hwy. 71 W., Ste 100, Austin, TX 78735). Dated/effective May 1, 2006. Signed by David A. Siekman, President (VIP), May 17, 2006; Barry N. Shamas, EVP (BNL), May 18, 2006.

**Scope:** VIP provides EDP services via its VIP System (New Business, Policy Admin, Agency Admin, Financial Admin, Claims, Vendor Provider, Transaction Tracking, Mail Tracking). BNL buys/maintains compatible equipment at its expense (¶1). Includes 1 data line and up to 70 devices (¶2A). VIP may enhance the system at its discretion and may change platform with reasonable written notice, paying BNL's resulting equipment/training costs (¶4I). BNL solely responsible for its own security choices and its people's acts (¶4F–H).

**Downtime/availability:** Downtime over 2 consecutive working days → VIP provides backup facility at its expense (¶3). System available 7:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. Central, Mon–Fri (¶12D). Daily off-site backups (BNL pays pro rata storage/transport); VIP maintains property insurance (¶12).

**Fees:**
- Minimum monthly fee $5,000 (¶5A).
- Schedule B: $.305 per policy per month, all BNL plans. Renewal policies (13+ months) billed annually/12, in advance monthly.
- New products/amended policies require a written addendum.
- Invoices due 10 days after postmark; late charge 1-1/2%/month or legal max, whichever is less.
- Extra line/adapter $200/mo; visual station $25; printer under 299 LPM $25; over 299 LPM $150.
- Pass-through expenses: forms, phone, travel (with prior written approval), postage, COM (approval needed).
- Payable in USD.
- Schedule A hourly rates: consultation/development/requirements/analysis $100; senior programmer $100; junior $85; computer time $150; termination services: consultation $100, programming $185, computer time $250; regulatory and non-standard processing computer time $150; education at VIP $50, on-site $90; phone help $50; bank drafts $.06 each.
- After the first 12 months, VIP may raise Schedule A rates on 30 days' notice, capped at 10% per year (¶14B).
- Data copies on termination: $100/hr programming, $150/hr processing (¶7D).

**Term/Termination:**
- Initial term 1 year from May 1, 2006. It then auto-renews year to year unless either party gives written notice at least 6 months before term end (¶15A–B).
- BNL terminating in an Extended Term with under 6 months' notice pays a cancellation fee: the greatest of (i) Minimum Fee × remaining months, (ii) average of the prior 6 months' billings × remaining months, or (iii) $30,000 (¶15C).
- For cause (¶7): nonpayment uncured 30 days after written notice (a disputed bill requires a meeting first); material breach uncured 30 days; insolvency/bankruptcy.
- BNL returns VIP software and manuals on termination.

**IP/Data:** VIP owns the VIP System. BNL gets a non-exclusive license during the term (¶13). BNL Data remains BNL's and is returned on termination. VIP may use it only for the services, except as required by law; VIP keeps work papers (¶6A). Confidentiality has standard exceptions.

**Warranties:** VIP warrants non-infringement of US patents and other IP, workmanlike performance, and no time-bomb code (¶9). It disclaims all other warranties, including merchantability and fitness (¶9E).

**Indemnity (¶8):** BNL indemnifies VIP for BNL's acts/omissions and information it provides. VIP indemnifies BNL for IP infringement (uncapped) and for VIP's acts/omissions (subject to the ¶9 limits). Indemnity survives termination.

**Liability caps:**
- Both parties exclude consequential, special, indirect and punitive damages.
- VIP's cap is fees paid in the 12 months before accrual for the specific service (in year one, the minimum fees for the first 12 months). Carve-outs: IP indemnity (¶8B) and data confidentiality (¶6A) (¶9F).
- BNL's cap is the same formula. Carve-outs: fees owed under ¶5, ¶15(a) and ¶15(c), and breach of VIP's proprietary rights (¶11).
- VIP is not liable for the causes in ¶9G, including BNL's erroneous data, third-party hardware/software, and BNL's failure to report errors timely.

**Disputes:** Oklahoma law. Binding AAA arbitration before 3 arbitrators (one chosen by each party, a neutral attorney chair appointed by the AAA), at a location the arbitrators designate. Injunctive relief is excluded from arbitration. The prevailing party recovers attorneys' fees (¶16C, E). Court venue: federal or state court in Austin, TX or Oklahoma City, OK (¶16G). Claims must be brought within 2 years of accrual (¶16M).

**Miscellaneous:**
- Assignment/subcontracting requires consent, not unreasonably withheld.
- Force majeure (¶16J) favors VIP only.
- Notices: hand delivery on receipt; certified mail deemed given "three (2) days" after mailing (internal inconsistency in the text); next-day courier on delivery.
- VIP may use BNL's name in advertising; other terms are confidential.
- Amendments must be in writing and signed.
- Entire agreement; no third-party beneficiaries; independent contractors; severability; non-waiver; VIP may serve other clients.

# Reference Notes: Maintenance and Support Agreement (VerticalNet / Converge)

**Parties/Dates:** VerticalNet, Inc. ("VNI") and VerticalNet Enterprises LLC (formerly Tradeum, Inc., d/b/a VerticalNet Solutions; "VNE"), together "Vert"; and Converge, Inc. Signed Oct 9, 2001; effective Oct 1, 2001. No amendments were provided. Companion: Amended and Restated Subscription License Agreement (SLA). Supported Products = SLA "Deployed Products," excluding the Structured Negotiations Product.

**Term (§9.1):** Initial Term to March 31, 2003. Renews only by mutual written agreement, up to three one-year Renewal Terms. Agreement continues for any unfinished Work Plan work. Renewal minimum fee is as mutually agreed (§4.2).

**Fees (§4):**
- Initial Term Minimum Fee $4,500,000, paid as 18 non-refundable monthly installments of $250,000. The first is due on execution; the rest by the 1st of each month (Nov 2001 through Mar 2003).
- Other amounts are invoiced monthly in arrears and due 30 days after receipt. Payment is in USD, with no setoff. Late charge is the lesser of 1.5% per month or the legal maximum.
- Quarterly Allocation (Exh. C): 1,920 estimated hours (12 weeks). All Problem Report support and Maintenance Updates are provided even if the allocation is exceeded. Support Requests and Professional Services beyond it are billed at VNE's then-current time charges, or per a Final SOW.
- Converge reimburses reasonable expenses, including travel. VNE bears travel for Error correction and travel it chooses to incur. Converge pays travel if remote access is unavailable.
- Sales taxes are on Converge. Withholding is handled per §4.7, with a gross-up if Converge reorganizes as a foreign person.

**Support (§2, Exh. A/B):**
- Converge provides Level 1 support; VNE provides Levels 2 and 3. Up to 7 Converge Support Personnel. Reporting is by phone (1-877-249-1423) or e-mail (support.solutions@verticalnet.com). Severity 1 and 2 must be reported by phone or in person.
- Support Hours are 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. ET on Support Days (Mon–Fri, excluding VNE holidays).
- Sev 1: response in 30 minutes (2 hours outside Support Hours); 24x7 effort; status every 24 hours; plan if no fix within 24 hours of diagnosis; final fix within 24 hours.
- Sev 2: response in 2 hours; diagnosis within 1 Support Day; status every other Support Day; plan at 48 hours; final fix in 72 hours.
- Sev 3: response by end of next Support Day; diagnosis within 2 Support Days; fix within 5 Support Days; weekly status.
- Sev 4: diagnosis commenced within 5 Support Days; resolved in a future Maintenance Update.
- VNE uses "reasonable best efforts." Converge pays if it requests a higher severity than proves actual, or if the Problem is not an Error.
- Converge should install Maintenance Updates within a reasonable time (expected ≤90 days). VNE provides weekly status logs. Modifications by Converge need 10 Business Days' notice, and VNE replies within 10 Business Days.

**Professional Services (§3):**
- Project Managers: Michael Decker (VNE), Farooq Ahmad (Converge). Relationship Managers: William Swank (VNE), Francesco DeMarchis (Converge), who must be director level or higher.
- "Environment and Deployment Process" document: draft within 30 days, Converge comments within 30 days, final within 90 days.
- Proposed SOW within 45 days of request. Change orders need both parties' signatures.
- Vert owns Converge-Requested Enhancements, except Converge-Independent Materials, Brand Features and Third-Party Materials. Vert gets an irrevocable, perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive license to those excluded items. No source code is owed to Converge unless the SLA says so.
- Delivery is to Massachusetts computers, with no tangible media.

**Warranty/Liability (§§5–6):**
- Services warranty is industry standard. Breach must be reported within 90 days; the sole remedy is repair, replacement or re-performance (within 30 days where feasible).
- Other warranties are disclaimed.
- Consequential damages are excluded.
- Cap: for Enhancements, amounts paid for that Enhancement; for Maintenance and Support, amounts paid in the preceding 3 months. The cap is collective for VNI/VNE and is in addition to fees owed.
- Carve-outs: bodily injury/property damage from willful misconduct or gross negligence, confidentiality breach, and court-added interest.
- Claims are routed to this Agreement or the SLA as §6.2 specifies. Parties have a duty to mitigate.

**Confidentiality (§7):** Reasonable care. The Agreement's terms are confidential. SEC filing requires redaction and a confidential treatment request, with 5 Business Days to identify redactions. There is no stated duration.

**Non-solicit (§8):** Term plus 1 year. It lapses as to VNE Service Personnel if Vert declines to renew (§9.5).

**Default/Termination (§9):**
- Events of Default: insolvency (involuntary petition undismissed for 60 days); material breach uncured 30 days (up to 60 if diligently curing); Converge non-payment uncured 3 Business Days after notice.
- Termination notice is due within 10 Business Days after the default.
- Automatic termination if the SLA terminates.
- Return or destroy Confidential Information, except as needed for surviving SLA licenses.

**General (§10):**
- Governing law: US and Pennsylvania law; CISG excluded; jury trial waived; claims must be brought within 2 years.
- Notices: VerticalNet, 507 Prudential Road, Horsham, PA 19044 (copy to Michael L. Pillion, Morgan, Lewis & Bockius, 1701 Market St., Philadelphia, PA 19103). Converge, Four Technology Drive, Peabody, MA 01960. Deemed given on personal delivery; courier on written verification of receipt; certified mail 5 days after deposit.
- Assignment is permitted to Affiliates; otherwise consent is required (not unreasonably withheld). A change of Control is not an assignment.
- Force majeure excludes payment obligations. Entire agreement includes the SLA. Amendments must be in a signed writing that references this Agreement.
